questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Afghanistan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Afghanistan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Afghanistan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Afghanistan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Afghanistan article.

questions.proof: It borders Pakistan in the south and east (border with India is disputed), Iran in the west, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in the north, and China in the far northeast.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Afghanistan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People and culture” part of the Afghanistan article.

questions.proof: Dari-Persian and Pashto are the two official languages of Afghanistan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Afghanistan is currently governed by the Taliban, after the collapse of the internationally recognized Islamic Republic of Afghanistan on 15 August _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Afghanistan article.

questions.proof: Afghanistan is currently governed by the Taliban, after the collapse of the internationally recognized Islamic Republic of Afghanistan on 15 August 2021.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The economy does not have growth (as April _____), of that kind that is called GDP growth, according to Worldbank.org.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Afghanistan article.

questions.proof: The economy does not have growth (as April 2024), of that kind that is called GDP growth, according to Worldbank.org.
